title: 2018 Honda Accord six-campaign recall retrieval pilot
evaluation_scope: Rank relevance to the text of owner symptoms among six model-year-listed campaign summaries; NOT VIN status or mechanical diagnosis
provenance: Manually paraphrased from public NHTSA recall reports and manufacturer notices; not a literal API payload and not independently expert-adjudicated

documents.text: A Honda Accord Body Control Module (BCM) software problem can interrupt communication with other systems. Possible malfunctions include windshield wipers, windshield defroster, rearview camera display, exterior lighting and turn indicators, audible warnings, and power windows. Honda's remedy is a BCM software update.

documents.component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
documents.text: For certain Honda Accord vehicles, the back-up camera center display or rearview camera image may fail to function in some situations. This can prevent the driver seeing behind the car when reversing. The remedy is to reprogram the display audio unit software.

Certain 2018-2019 Honda Accord vehicles have a low-pressure fuel pump motor defect. The fuel pump impeller may swell, the pump may seize and stop, and the engine may not start or may stall while driving, causing loss of drive power. The remedy is replacement of the fuel pump motor.

Certain Honda vehicles including some Accord variants may have an improperly molded fuel-pump impeller that deforms. Fuel pump failure can prevent starting, cause engine hesitation, loss of drive power or engine stalling while driving. A check engine light may illuminate. The remedy is fuel pump module replacement; exact VIN eligibility must be checked.

Certain 2018-2019 Honda Accord front seat belt buckles may not latch properly because a buckle channel interferes with the release button. A belt that fails to latch cannot restrain the occupant in a crash. Dealers inspect and replace the buckle release button or buckle assembly.

The front passenger seat weight sensor printed circuit board can crack and short circuit after humidity exposure. The passenger occupant classification system may fail; the SRS warning light may illuminate and the passenger airbag could deploy inappropriately during a crash, including with a child occupant. The remedy is replacing the seat weight sensor.
